The provided javadoc is for the two-argument version but the one-argument version also throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if the begin index is negative or greater than the string length. - The first call occurs inside `while (resPath.startsWith("//"))`. Since the string starts with "//", its length is at least 2, so begin index 1 is always valid. After each removal, the string remains starting with a single slash (if originally more slashes) but never violates the condition.
- The second call occurs inside `while (resPath.endsWith("/"))`. Since the string ends with "/", its length is at least 1, so end index `length-1` is non-negative and less than length, and begin index 0 is valid. After removal, the new string may still end with "/" if multiple trailing slashes, but again the indices remain valid.
- There is no other call to `substring`. Therefore, all implicit preconditions are satisfied by the loop guards, and `IndexOutOfBoundsException` is avoided.
